terra.problem: The king accuses them of conspiring to speak false words, not of already speaking dishonestly.
The king says they conspired to speak false words; the text does not say he accuses them of already being dishonest.
The text does not say Arioch is at Daniel's door or that Daniel does not panic.
Saying Daniel is not hunting for someone to blame adds an unstated intention.
The text says men went looking for Daniel and his friends; it does not identify them as soldiers.
The passage says Daniel blessed God, but does not establish that praise was the first thing out of his mouth.
The passage does not establish that the events before the nighttime vision all happened on the same day.
The text does not mention a scroll or note, but it does not establish that Daniel made neither.
The text says Daniel declared these words, but does not say he addressed this part of his praise to God.
Daniel speaks up for the wise men, but the text does not say at this point that he has saved them.
The joke about the chapter being shorter makes the way Scripture is written the joke.
Calling the feet the statue's weak spot adds an identification the dream does not make.
The cookie jar comparison does not match the action of a stone striking the statue's feet.
The text does not say the stone was small.
Saying the kingdom has no gentle side goes beyond the text's statement that it will shatter and crush the other kingdoms.
The text says God's kingdom will bring the other kingdoms to an end, not that every kingdom in the statue gets replaced.
The passage does not establish that the king's reaction happened on a day with an earlier morning.
The text does not say the king's anger was hours earlier.
The passage does not say Daniel stood outside waiting for Arioch.
The explanation identifies Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego as the three friends without citing Daniel 1:6–7, which connects their names.
